articles.title: Anthony Bourdain’s Kitchen Confidential Gets Deluxe Folio Society Release
articles.summary: Anthony Bourdain's iconic memoir Kitchen Confidential is getting a new edition from The Folio Society, and it includes an exclusive portrait of the late, great chef from the one and only Paul Pope.
articles.body:
When it comes to writing about food with wit and candor, few can rival the late, great Anthony Bourdain. Bourdain's memoir Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly remains a giant in the genre, and it's only fitting that the book is joining the ever-growing library of deluxe hardcover editions at The Folio Society.

One of the many perks of The Folio Society's edition of Kitchen Confidential is that it includes a portrait of Bourdain commissioned from his friend, legendary artist Paul Pope. IGN can exclusively debut that image below:

Here's the official summary of what to expect from this edition of Kitchen Confidential:

The Folio Society edition of Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly features a cover, slipcase and endpapers designed by Kishan Rajani, incorporating Jake Chessum’s photography on the cover as well as an adapted food list in Bourdain's handwriting on the slipcase. The edition includes 12 stunning, rare photos by Chessum, a photographer whose extensive portfolio includes definitive imagery of Bill Gates, Kate Moss, Brad Pitt, The Strokes, Amy Winehouse, and President Obama. The book also features gilded edges, blocked cloth binding, and a generous cookbook-style format, making the most of the integrated photographs which mostly appear as double-page spreads. The book also includes an all-new illustration of Bourdain by the bestselling, award-winning artist Paul Pope, which was commissioned specifically for this edition.

“Tony was a special person and I'm glad I got to know him and work with him,” said Pope in a statement. “I wanted to evoke his young days with a bit of an expressionist/punk portrait combining lower east side New York and the music which he loved. Bourdain forever forever Bourdain.”

“Told in Bourdain’s signature exhilarating, full-throttle, and sharply funny style, Kitchen Confidential remains so compelling after all these years because its pages teem with the authenticity, passion, and generosity of spirit of its iconic author,” said editor Mandy Kirkby. “Restaurant kitchen culture has changed since its writing, but some things remain: brunch is usually a rip off, chicken is for scaredy cats and the undiscerning, and shellfish is a bad idea in an empty restaurant, whatever the day of the week. It’s not a cookbook—and not even a book about food, per se—but it will definitely leave you feeling hungry.”

The Folio Society's Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly - Image Gallery

This edition of Kitchen Confidential is priced at £85 / US $130 and will go on sale at 8am PT on October 13 on the Folio Society website .

Bourdain's legacy also lives on in the form of Get Jiro, a new Adult Swim animated series based on his graphic novel series. You can check out IGN's review of the Get Jiro series premiere .

articles.title: Valor Mortis Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: Valor Mortis from developer One More Level is a bold departure for the studio and genre as a whole.
articles.body:
Valor Mortis from developer One More Level is a bold departure for the studio and genre as a whole.

A first-person Soulslike, Valor Mortis is a slower, measured take for a studio best known for its speedy, first-person parkour action in the beloved Ghostrunner series.

There are familiar trappings in the Soulslike here, of course. But there are also some unexpected twists in exploration, an engrossing setting and interesting progression systems at play that truly help Valor Mortis stand out from the pack before launch.

NFL Season Shaping Up To Be Unpredictable 🗣️

A historical Eastern European setting besieged by a plague is suddenly one of the more captivating backdrops for a game in recent memory.

This era has been done before, no doubt, but the supernatural twist on top of the fighting in realistic, grisly displays of violence and superb sound design really makes Valor Mortis feel distinct.

Truly, there are few more interesting settings in games right now. What could have been a by-the-books historical romp instead has players stumbling upon odd growths throughout the landscape, grotesque monsters and so much more. There are landmarks aplenty, and it all makes even backtracking fun.

A blade is the weapon of choice here. In an interesting twist on the expected gameplay tropes for the genre, players will sacrifice a little health to perform a block. There's a risk-reward there, plus needing to properly read a foe's intentions, as a dodge will get them past unblockable attacks and parries, as expected, reward proper timing with big counter damage.

There's a little era-specific range involved too courtesy of a firearms. Ammo is super scarce at times, but for good reason: Players can use this to target enemy weak points, leading to staggers.

Leaning into the supernatural slant of the whole thing, players also get magic-like abilities dubbed "transmutations" that add another layer of strategy to the combat. It feels a little generic to call it Bioshock-like, but that's what it is and it feels great.

Valor Mortis goes the expected genre route with death, too, respawning players at the last checkpoint visited, but this time it's lanterns. Enemies respawn too.

Where the game veers away from others, though, is a Metroidvania-like revisiting feel. As players unlock new abilities, new spots in already-explored areas open up, as do new discoverable items and, of course, enemies.

A heavy emphasis on exploration is a welcome surprise. The combat feels great, but getting to explore the world so much is a nice bonus that breaks up the pacing really well.

With an alternate 1820 Eastern Europe setting, Valor Mortis was already pretty unique with just that going for it. Add a supernatural element and things just go over the top.

It's engrossing, with whispers in the narrative of Napoleon's Battle of Waterloo victory being fueled by a mysterious substance that makes his soldiers die more than once for him.

Players take on the role of a resurrected William, who must confront undead comrades and other memorable (or haunting) things out in the world. Players get wrapped up in conspiracies, mysteries and quite a bit more over the course of what is a pretty lengthy, strong story.

Overall progression gets a nice boost from the "catalysts" earned, enabling base stat upgrades to things like health. The fun wrinkle there is that players must spend them, as unspent catalysts get dropped upon death and gone forever.

Layering atop that nicely are "ambers," little add-ons to a build players can equip every five levels earned. It gives players some agency over what sort of style they want to take.

Overall, Valor Mortis runs well amid all the chaos it presents and the options feature plenty of tweakable things for players to tinker with as needed.

Valor Mortis presents a captivating world that serves as one of the most memorable settings in modern games.

Beyond that, the strong combat from the first-person perspective is a must-have genre twist that's done very well. Difficulty can be uneven at times, but staples of the genre, like learning enemy patterns and improving by the battle, are all there.

The fact exploration of the world is enjoyable to the point that even backtracking can be fun is really just an exclamation point, cementing Valor Mortis as one of the best surprises of the year.

articles.title: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction Release Date Confirmed
articles.summary: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction has a release date: February 4, 2027.
articles.body:
Bitmap Bureau, the developer behind Terminator 2D: No Fate, worked with Mattel and the retro team at Clear River Games on the old-school brawler, which launches digitally and physically on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. Two physical versions of the game will be available via Limited Run Games. The standard physical release costs $29.99, and the Collector’s Edition costs $99.99.

Dragon Pearl of Destruction is inspired by the much-loved ‘80s animated series, and you can see that come through in pixel-art and 2D gameplay. The playable characters are He-Man, She-Ra, Man-At-Arms, and Teela, and you can play solo or co-op (two-player local co-op).

There are 13 stages, including the Royal Palace, the Vine Jungle, and Snake Mountain, and famous villains such as Skeletor, Evil-Lyn, Beast Man, and Trap Jaw. You’ll also bump into the dark sorceress Shokoti and the Shadow Beasts.

The Collector’s Edition includes lunchbox style packaging, pin badges, a mini-power sword, and an acrylic standee featuring He-Man riding Battle Cat, among other things. The contents of both physical editions are detailed below.

articles.title: Movie Retailer Zavvi Warns Customers to Stop Buying From Its Site as It Enters Administration
articles.summary: Movie retailer Zavvi has entered administration, a legal concept similar to bankruptcy, and has warned customers not to place new orders.
articles.body:
Movie retailer Zavvi has entered administration, a legal concept similar to bankruptcy, and has warned customers not to place new orders.

Zavvi was an entertainment retailer, similar to FYE, in the UK during the late 2000s, which shut down all of its physical stores. However, the brand stayed alive via a website which was well-respected by physical media collectors. Zavvi has long carried a large collection of Blu-rays and 4K movies, including sought after steelbooks. Unfortunately, the website appears to be on death's door.

Zavvi has announced that it is entering administration. As a result, it will not be able to fulfill outstanding orders and preorders, and the company has told customers to speak with their banks to get their money back. Additionally, although the website remains active, the company is warning customers not to make any new purchases either.

Administration doesn't mean that Zavvi will die forever. It's a process that attempts to give companies a path back to sustainability. However, it remains to be seen if that will happen for Zavvi. If the company can't get out of this, it will be a blow to physical media lovers. The options for purchasing new Blu-rays and steelbooks have shrunk radically over the last six years or so. Major retailers like Target and Best Buy no longer sell films in-store and enthusiast websites like Zavvi are now at risk of ceasing to exist.

articles.title: The Folio Society's Japanese Ghost Stories Hardcover Is the Perfect Halloween Companion
articles.summary: The classic horror collection Japanese Ghost Stories is getting a deluxe new hardcover edition from The Folio Society, and we have an exclusive preview of some of the haunting illustrations.
articles.body:
The Folio Society's newest release is one that should appeal to fans of classic horror stories. Lafcadio Hearn's short story collection Japanese Ghost Stories is getting a lavish new hardcover edition, featuring illustrations by The Unwritten's Yuko Shimizu.

With Japanese Ghost Stories going up for preorder soon, IGN can exclusively debut some of Shimizu's gorgeous illustrations. Check them out in the slideshow gallery below:

The Folio Society's Japanese Ghost Stories Image Gallery

Japanese Ghost Stories features a translation by Royall Tyler and a new introduction by Japanese novelist Yoko Ogawa. Here's the official description of the book:

JAPANESE GHOST STORIES features twenty transportive and sometimes terrifying tales, including “The Story of Aoyagi,” in which a young samurai falls in love with a mysterious woman only to discover she is not what she seems; “Oshidori,” the haunting tale in which a mandarin duck mourns the loss of her lover, who was shot and killed by a hunter’ “The Dream of Akinosuké,” in which a man becomes the king of an ant kingdom; and “Rokuro-Kubi,” an action packed story in which a monk battles five flying heads.

In JAPANESE GHOST STORIES, the dead wreak revenge on the living, paintings come alive, spectral brides possess mortal men and a priest devours human flesh. These tales draw on the phantoms and ghouls of traditional Japanese folklore—including the headless 'rokuro-kubi', the monstrous goblins 'jikininki' and the faceless 'mujina' who stalk lonely neighbourhoods. The stories are massively popular in Japan and highly regarded by folklore aficionados and horror enthusiasts alike.

“Lafcadio Hearn's 19th-century ghost stories are famous throughout Japan and are part of that country's culture of the supernatural. I love the way we've taken something traditional and given it a modern twist,” said Folio Society Editor Mandy Kirby in a statement. “At first glance, you might think Yuko Shimizu's illustrations are from the time of Hokusai, but look closer and you can see that they have modern touches, and the cover is unmistakably 21st century. One of Japan's contemporary novelists, Yoko Ogawa, has provided an introduction in which she talks about Japan's obsession with ghosts and demons, and how unsettling and scary these stories actually are. She's right - they are absolute gems of the supernatural, the perfect read for the ghostly season."

Orders for Japanese Ghost Stories will open on the Folio Society website on October 13.

In other Folio Society news, the company is also releasing a stunning new edition of Anthony Bourdain's classic memoir Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly .

articles.title: Mechanism’s first Switch 2 case is as awesome as I hoped it would be
articles.summary: While most companies have slowed down with new Nintendo Switch 2 cases, Mechanism recently launched its first. And it’s great.
articles.body: Most companies have slowed down releasing new Switch 2 cases, but one of my favorite accessory makers recently debuted its first, after a few delays. The $49 Basecase from Mechanism is a snap-on shell for the console that taps into the company’s modular lineup of mounts. You could already mount the Switch 2 in numerous ways with its $19 Basegrip (to your wall, to its Gaming Pillow, to a monitor arm, etc.). The difference is that this new product protects your console, makes its Joy-Con more comfortable to use, and has some interesting modularity. The console shell allows for the full range of the Switch 2’s kickstand, and access to all of the ports, buttons, and fan vents. Notably, it fits more snugly than others I’ve tried because it clamps on near the console’s bottom USB-C port. This is a good thing. You can unlock its rear plate and replace it with a custom 3D-printed version for more fun and/or more utility. Mechanism sent over a couple of printed examples that hint at the possibilities — one that has Lego pegs on it for sticking on some minifigures, and another that has crannies for game cartridges. [Image: [Image: The grips that slide onto the back of the Joy-Con protectors are modular, too. The set includes two sizes that add varying degrees of bulk, both of which make them more comfortable to use. Remove any of the grips, and there’s a spot for a game cartridge. It’s a fun way to bring extra physical games. Mechanism included some extra grip types that aren’t for sale to show what’s possible with a 3D printer. I really liked the pair that has a little shelf on each side to let your middle or ring fingers rest. You can’t use the Switch 2 in its dock with the Basecase. So, Mechanism includes a dock adapter that takes a different approach — not necessarily better or worse — than Dbrand did with its Killswitch. Instead of cradling the Switch 2, it’s simply a female-to-male USB-C cable that you have to maneuver onto the dock’s video-out port. Installing it isn’t quite as easy as its marketing indicates, but I eventually got it working. Those who use a third-party USB-C dock from Jsaux or Genki won’t need to use this component. [Image: [Image: The Basecase seems designed to address multiple points of failure in earlier Switch 2 cases released by Dbrand, Genki, and others that unfortunately let some quality control issues slip in an effort to launch cases first when the Swtich 2 first debuted. For instance, the Basecase’s Joy-Con grips have a little rubber lip that fits around the top of the controller’s inner colored section. Dbrand revised its comfy Killswitch grip to add this after some users noted their consoles tumbling to the ground when they grabbed it by the controller without supporting the Switch 2’s weight. The Basecase does a good job of preventing this issue. Also important: the swappable Joy-Con grips attach easily, requiring almost no effort to line up the latch pins to snap on. I could never quite get the feel for the ones included with Genki’s Attack Vector case (we’ll see how Genki’s upcoming Grips fare). Also, while most thin, plastic cases from competitors exhibit ill-fitting sections or flex, the Basecase feels tougher. If you’re bought into Mechanism’s ecosystem of mounts and have a Switch 2, there’s a good chance that you’ve been waiting for this release (and, perhaps, you already own this case). For gamers who haven’t yet tried out the company’s system of mounts, this is a really good place to start. You can grab all of the 3D printer files at Makerworld or Printables. Photography by Cameron Faulkner/The Verge

articles.body:
Universal has revealed first-look pictures of Miami Vice '85 showing Michael B. Jordan as Ricardo Tubbs and Austin Butler as James 'Sonny' Crockett.

The reboot for the classic '80s show, which has been in the works from Top Gun: Maverick director Joseph Kosinski since last year, eased movie fans into Monday with two photos of its stars ahead of its release in 2028. These first photos show Jordan and Butler as their slick title characters, guns in hand.

Both images were shared on social media to celebrate the start of production, meaning there's still plenty of work to do to bring it all together before its big premiere in a few years. You can see both Jordan as Tubbs and Butler as Crockett below.

Michael B. Jordan is Tubbs. Austin Butler is Crockett. Miami Vice ’85 - now in production.

Per Variety , a description for Miami Vice '85 says the reboot will explore "the glamour and corruption of mid-80's Miami." Its story is "inspired by the pilot episode and first season of the landmark television series that influenced culture and set the style of everything from fashion to filmmaking."

Despite being nearly two years away from speeding onto movie screens, this latest swing at a Miami Vice movie has amassed quite the cast. The Odyssey and original Miami Vice show star John Leguizamo was reportedly cast as the new film's main villain back in September . Fallout and The White Lotus actor Walton Goggins was reportedly added as a second villain just a few weeks ago.

Miami Vice '85 is set to premiere May 19, 2028 . It's produced by Kosinski and Dylan Clark (The Batman), with Dan Gilroy and Eric Singer attached as writers.

For more, you can read up on the 2006 movie starring Colin Farrell and Jamie Foxx. IGN gave it an 8/10 review back at the time of its release, saying, "for those seeking an intense, seductive and gritty crime drama, Miami Vice delivers the goods."

articles.title: Biohazard Exclusive Teaser Trailer: Chandler Riggs' Resident Evil 7 Fan Film - IGN
articles.summary: Ethan Winters, while searching for his missing wife, finds himself trapped by the Baker family - a deadly, unstoppable family driven to violence under the influence of a mysterious infection.BIOHAZARD is a short fan film based on the critically acclaimed video game Resident Evil 7, written, directed, and starring Chandler Riggs (The Walking Dead). The film reunites Riggs with Jason Douglas (The Walking Dead, Preacher, Dragon Ball), who portrays Jack Baker - the patriarch of this twisted family - alongside Mary Rachel Quinn (Outer Banks), Eugenie Bondurant (The Conjuring: The Devil Made Me Do It, The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 2), Johnathan O’Neil (The Pitt), and newcomer Sam Coyles.BIOHAZARD began as a passion project driven by a desire to bring the isolated, intense, gripping story of Resident Evil 7 into live-action. The production team spent days transforming Arturo Fuente’s original cigar factory in Tampa Bay into a full-scale section of the Baker estate, creating a practical, immersive environment specifically for the production. articles.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother Cast on Preparing for Their Intense Roles | IGN Fall Fan Fest 2026
articles.body:
Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother is the intense story of a hitman Latif (played by Mahershala Ali) struggling after the death of his wife with caring for his family, and wrestling with his faith. As part of IGN Fall Fan Fest 2026, John Cho, who plays a somewhat unhinged pastor, and Adia, who plays Latif's daughter, sat down with IGN to discuss how they prepared for filming such emotionally demanding roles.

John Cho's Christian pastor is a complicated antagonist with good intentions but extremist methods, and his character is particularly notable for his combination of cowboy fashion and gold grills. Cho explained how the character's unique look came about.

"It was definitely a collaborative process. I didn't know what he was gonna look like. This is pretty unique in the work that I've done on film where very little was obvious to me on the page," he says. "I didn't know what he looked like or sounded like. Should he have an accent? Should he not? All of those things were undecided for me, and we just came in and started working.

"Deirdra [Elizabeth Govan], our costume designer, started suggesting things, and I didn't know. I know she thinks that I was giving her side-eye, but I was really unsure."

The character's look eventually came together through key elements like cowboy boots and a hat, resulting in a portrayal that's very different from what fans of Cho might be used to.

"For me, the big pieces were, by the end, two things. It was the shirt that commemorated his mother's passing… it was like my superhero outfit, you know? And then the grills, which really took me out of my head and gave me a piece of character history. When I looked in the mirror, I was like, Okay, that's not me. That's definitely not me ."

While Cho's character serves as an antagonist to Latif throughout the movie, Latif's daughter Fatiha tries to support her father and brother while also grieving the loss of her mother. It's an intense role, and Adia revealed that she created a diary for her character to help develop a deeper understanding of Fatiha's experiences.

"I had a journal that I would keep with me," she says. "I did this timeline for myself, but then I also did a lot of journaling in her voice to pull out what some of her thoughts might be in that moment in time that we are finding her, but even the times before we meet her in the film and after. There's so much, there's a lot of depth going on there in terms of dealing with hormones, puberty, your mother passing, and dealing with all of that.

"Then when we got to the actual set and we were actually shooting, I really had to work on letting go of all of that and trusting that my prep work would have a beautiful undercurrent to whatever I was presenting in the moment, so that I could just be present with whatever I was doing for that day."

Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother is in US theaters now and you can check out IGN's review of the movie, which we gave an 8.

articles.title: The Pikachu and Poké Ball LEGO Set Has Hit Its Lowest Price Yet at Amazon With $13 Discount
articles.summary: The LEGO Pokémon Pikachu and Poké Ball set has dropped to its lowest price yet at Amazon of $186.99, a $13 discount off its full price.
articles.body:
It's been an exciting year for Pokémon fans celebrating the franchise's 30th anniversary. If you're not tracking down some of the new 30th Celebration TCG drops to buy, there have been LEGO sets galore to look into building, including an absolutely adorable set of Pikachu and a Poké Ball .

If you've been eager to add this 2,050-piece display to your collection, this is a great time to check it out. Amazon's knocked $13 off its price tag, dropping it down to $186.99 from its MSRP of $199.99. It may not be a massive discount, but it is the lowest price we've seen on it so far at the retailer, which is well worth looking into while it's still live.

This delightful display piece released towards the start of this year in February and is quite a big undertaking with its 2,050 bricks, so it makes sense why it's angled towards adult builders . With all of those pieces, you'll create a ridiculously cute Pikachu figure (with posable ears and limbs) leaping from an opened Poké Ball. Or, if you'd prefer a more neutral pose, there's also the option to pose Pikachu just resting by a closed Poké Ball instead.

If you decide to do the former pose, there's quite a fun base you'll get to build for the big leap. Of course, it's shaped like a lightning bolt for this Electric-type Pokémon, and features the number "25" in LEGO studs on the bottom, which is a nice little nod to Pikachu's Pokédex number.

articles.title: VisionQuest Release Schedule Reveals Early Premiere for Episode 1
articles.summary: Marvel has published the full release schedule for VisionQuest, revealing an early premiere for Episode 1.
articles.body:
Marvel has published the full release schedule for VisionQuest , revealing an early premiere for Episode 1.

The Vision (Paul Bettany) and Ultron-led (James Spader) Disney+ show's rollout plan materialized on Marvel Studios social media channels today – and it came with a bit of a surprise. Instead of starting its offshoot story on October 14 as originally planned , VisionQuest Episode 1 will arrive tomorrow, October 13, at 6pm PT / 9pm ET.

It's a one-day-early premiere that Marvel waited to announce until today, and it came with more specific information about the full release plan, too. Those hoping to keep up with VisionQuest can expect two episodes each week until its penultimate episode arrives alone November 3, with the eighth and final episode then arriving one week after that. You can see the full breakdown below.

Episode 1: "No Strings" and Episode 2: "Theseus" – October 13

Episode 3: "Reboot" and Episode 4: "Malware" – October 20

Episode 5: "Firewall" and Episode 6: "Deadlock" – October 27

"Vision, rebooted and having escaped from those who sought to weaponize him, has been in hiding," an official synopsis for the show says. "Searching for new meaning, he consults the AI personas embedded in his programming, including Friday, Edith, Jarvis, and the infamous Ultron. His discreet existence ends when a bounty placed on his head thrusts him on the run with Thomas Shepard, a mysterious boy who may be Vision’s son, reincarnate."

VisionQuest will wrap up the WandaVision trilogy through the course of the next few weeks. It should provide a nice distraction as Marvel Cinematic Universe fans await the next big event film, Avengers: Doomsday , December 18, 2026.

articles.summary: IGN can exclusively reveal Godzilla Versus Everything, a massive new crossover event that may well be IDW's most ambitious Godzilla comic ever.
articles.body:
IDW has been busy establishing an ambitious new Godzilla line with the Kai-Sei Universe , which kicked off in 2025. Now, IGN can exclusively reveal that the Kai-Sei line will experience its first major crossover event in 2027.

The crossover in question is dubbed Godzilla Versus Everything. This four-issue miniseries sees Godzilla achieve his newest and most powerful form, forcing the casts of the flagship Godzilla comic, The Deadzone, Starship Godzilla, and The Horror of Godzilla to band together to save humanity.

Godzilla Versus Everything is written by Tim Seeley and illustrated by Fero Pe. Here's the official description for the series:

From New York Times bestselling writer Tim Seeley and acclaimed artist Fero Pe comes GODZILLA VS EVERYTHING, the first four-issue crossover event from the celebrated Kai-Sei era line of comics at IDW Publishing. Since the Kai-Sei era made its unforgettable debut in 2025, everything in the connected universe of comics - GODZILLA, STARSHIP GODZILLA, DEADZONE, and THE HORROR OF GODZILLA - has been building up to this jaw-dropping blockbuster. Godzilla has achieved its most powerful form yet and has its sights set on destroying the world. Can the combined forces of Earth - and beyond - stop the King of the Monsters, or will Godzilla finally destroy the world?

"When I started work with editor Jake Williams and IDW on GODZILLA, the big pitch was this was going to play like a universe of titles, but also as a universe of characters,” said Seeley in a statement. “From the beginning, the goal was they'd all come together at some point as friends and/or enemies in a proper comic universe event title. Well, we're here, and all the meticulous plotting of our creative crew leads to a wild, weird, terrifying crossover comic that puts Godzilla, the kaiju and our cast through every epic story beat you've ever wanted."

Godzilla Versus Everything #1 will debut in March 2027. Fans can also look forward to a lead-in to the crossover in March's Godzilla #17, which will be the final issue of the series. The buildup begins this month in Starship Godzilla: Invasion X #1, Godzilla: Revenge of the Deadzone #1, and Godzilla #13. You can preorder all of these comics at your local comic shop .

articles.title: Every Magic: The Gathering Set Confirmed for 2027, Including Marvel: Darkhold Destiny
articles.summary: Wizards of the Coast is scaling back to six Magic: The Gathering sets in 2027. Here is the full schedule, including Kamigawa, Zhalfir, and what we could expect from Universes Beyond
articles.body:
So much has been made of Universes Beyond, Magic: The Gathering’s crossovers with other IP, that many have dubbed the game “the Fortnite of card games”.

2026 saw seven sets in a single calendar year, which means that—at the time of writing—we’re closing in on November's release of Star Trek. In 2027, though, things are changing — not only is Wizards of the Coast cutting the number of sets down to six (with three Universes Within and three Universes Beyond), but we won’t get a back-to-back of Universes Beyond at all. Hooray!

Here’s all we know about Magic’s 2027 sets so far, and what to expect from them, including the recently revealed Marvel: Darkhold Destiny .

The first set of 2027 will debut in early February, and it’ll take us to Nauctis. This “Sunken Realm” is all about being under the waves, so you can expect some deep-sea humans alongside merfolk, homarids, and seals.

Here’s Wizards of the Coast’s synopsis: “As tensions bubble between two warring kingdoms, a group of unlikely heroes must rise to the occasion—or their home will be swallowed up by the abyssal depths of the ocean. Adventures await under the water, and players will come face to face with fearsome creatures that dwell far, far from the surface.”

We knew we'd be getting more Marvel sets, but we didn't quite expect the spooky Darkhold Destiny to arrive before something like the X-Men.

Still, this time things are a little different: This is based on an original story, rather than just dragging Marvel characters into Magic.

Expect four Commander Decks, two Scene Boxes, Play Boosters, Bundles, and yes, those all-important Collector Boosters.

2026 saw two trips back to iconic planes with Lorwyn and Strixhaven, and in 2027 we’re heading back to Kamigawa.

The cyberpunk-infused setting will see a huge shift when the Ikoria plane crashes into it, leading to a mechs versus kaiju set.

“Return to Kamigawa and harness the power of next-generation mechs that can match the might of any titan. The Kamigawans will need all the help they can get, because the behemoths of Ikoria may be the greatest threat this plane has ever seen.”

“And if you'd rather be the monster than fight them, you can harness your favorite creatures from Ikoria in the battle for the city. Suit up, get ready to rumble, and witness a battle on a scale you've never seen before.”

Zhalfir sounds a lot like it’ll be a love letter to longtime Magic fans, arriving as its own plane and bringing back the legendary chronomancer, Teferi Akosa.

It’ll lean into the afrofantasy subgenre, but we don’t know much else about it just yet.

“Immerse yourself in the beauty of Zhalfir and harness innovative new forms of magic. The minds behind this plane have crafted some especially mind-bending cards, each embracing the unique visual design of Magic's take on the afrofantasy genre.”

“And because Zhalfir is so closely tied to an era of Magic that many players hold dear, we're honoring its legacy in every aspect of the set. This is Magic: The Gathering as you remember it, crafted with the love and care of our contemporary design philosophy.”

We are yet to have anything confirmed for 2027 Universes Beyond beyond the new Marvel Darkhold Destiny set, but that won't stop us speculating on what could be in store. For now, we have the dates in which we should expect the three sets.

Beyond that, if you'll pardon the pun, the only piece of info we have is from Hasbro CEO Chris Cocks notes in the recent earnings report . Cocks noted feedback on recent Universes Beyond sets, which have run the gamut from two trips to Middle-Earth, just as many visits to New York City, every single Final Fantasy, and, soon, Star Trek.

“The one thing I'll say on the Universes Beyond partners that we have next year is they'll probably be a bit more fantasy-adjacent," he explained.

"And I don't think any of them will take place in New York City because we definitely have gotten that feedback from some fans."

From that, there are a lot of potential crossovers that would be fun for Magic: The Gathering, but the idea of refocusing on fantasy IP certainly is interesting.

We've recently predicted it could be anything from Games of Thrones, to Elden Ring, Warhammer: Age of Sigmar, The Legend of Zelda, The Witcher, or World of Warcraft. But, that's purely speculation, and we shall have to wait and see what is officially announced later this year.

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: Resident Evil Requiem’s Stars: Leon Fever, Crucial Character Moments, and Apocalypse Advice | IGN Fall Fan Fest 2026
articles.body:
Resident Evil has always been huge with gamers, but Resident Evil Requiem is the biggest-selling installment yet. For Fall Fan Fest 2026, IGN spoke to the actors behind Grace Ashcroft and Leon S. Kennedy, Angela Sant'Albano and Nick Apostolides, about their experiences creating their characters and what they've made of the enthusiastic, and sometimes feral, fan reaction since launch.

"Nick has been wonderful. He's been like a big brother in a way, kind of guiding me through it all," says Sant'Albano of taking her first step into the world of Resident Evil.

"It was hard to sum up what those guys were about to get into," said Apostolides of his role as a series veteran, having starred in the remakes of Resident Evil 2 and 4 and Netflix's Resident Evil: Infinite Darkness.

"I knew because of my history with the franchise. I'd already done three projects with it, and I had an intimate understanding of the fanbase and how excited and passionate they are. So I was just secretly excited for these guys," he said. "I think I just tried to help everyone understand the grim universe that they were stepping into, because these games are fun, they're campy at times, and yes, they're about zombies and surviving and the apocalypse, but they also have such grounded reality to them. They center around real human stories, and so: not psyching them out, but getting them prepared for what they're about to experience."

Part of what makes Resident Evil Requiem such a standout for the series are the characters of Grace, a young woman suddenly facing not just grief, but monsters and the contrast with an older, wiser, veteran of the world, Leon. Apostolides picked out the scene that, for him, really encapsulated the version of Leon that we see in Resident Evil Requiem.

"There was a scene that really reinforced what Leon is all about. When he's in the garbage dump area with Grace. Grace is sitting by his side, and then he gets up, and Grace asks him, 'You're so sick; why do you keep going? You're not going to make it.' And he just says a few select keywords here: 'I couldn't make a difference back then. But I'm here now, and this is my chance to make a difference.' And that's what he's all about. That's his spine, that's his DNA; he just wants to do the right thing and help those who can't help themselves. He's always been that guy, and even facing the end possibly, he's still doing that."

For Sant'Albano, the scene that really stood out to her from Grace's story was is her reaction to the death of her mother. "You understand the sort of trauma that she went through. Grace, I think from from birth, is introverted and a little uncomfortable with human contact and all that good stuff. I think from seeing her mother pass away in such a traumatic way, it sort of exacerbated all everything for her," she said.

"And then the other one, which made me understand Grace's journey and the courage that she had to find, was actually when Emily died, because you understood, first of all, the guilt that Grace had. Because I think there's a line where she literally says again, 'This is how I've done this again. This is all my fault.' And you understand this burden and this guilt that she's carried her whole life.

"That feeling that she let her mom down, and now she's letting this other person she's really grown to love and care about down. But I also think it made it very clear to me of where I had to get to in terms of Grace's journey. She has to stand up for someone else, and even though she's not good at standing up for herself, she has to find that bravery."

The fanbase turned out to be especially excited for Leon S. Kennedy this time around. He's always been an attractive male lead, but something about the more mature, slightly grizzled version of him that appeared in Requiem sent certain corners of the internet feral, complete with Instagram thirst traps.

"You know, it's funny, I was kind of expecting the status quo. He was always popular. He's a great-looking character. He stands for such good in the world, but it was a whole different level of… What's the word I'm looking for?"

"Okay, it was a whole different level of Leon fever that I was not expecting. It was dialed up to, like, a 12. And I thought it was going to be, like, a nine, so we'll say that."

One of the big obsessions after the game was released is that one version of Leon was wearing a wedding ring, but the game didn't reveal who the lucky Mrs. S. Kennedy was. Both stars say they get asked all the time by fans.

"They're asking me as if I know," says Apostolides. "I usually just say he's married to you, the fans."

After the positive reaction to the game and renewed interest, even outside the world of games, thanks to the new movie, what is it about the series that gives it a longevity beyond so many other horror games and zombie stories?

"I feel like Capcom is just dialed in," says Apostolides. "Number one, I think they really, really do listen to the fans. They also know what they're doing. They're extremely talented. And that's what separates the franchises from the ones that survive all these years and the ones that kind of flutter out.

"I think it's also a perfect recipe for these projects and these games, where, yes, it's about zombies, killing zombies, stopping world domination from evil corporations, but it's also centered around human stories that — the fans get so attached to these characters, and they feel like they're surviving a huge obstacle together with their friends, with the people that they watch, with the characters. And there's — I think there's a beautiful, like, metaphor to life of just getting through adversity."

"For me, like, as an actor, when I first read the script, I just felt that the human story is what made the game so addictive," adds Sant'Albano. "And with Leon, just the fact that they managed to create such a beloved character so early on. It's really a testament to the fans of, you know, staying with the game and watching Leon grow older and meet new characters and see where life takes him. But I think creating complex characters like Grace, that's just so delicious for a gamer or for anyone, frankly, in any medium, is to have a really complex character that they can observe."

Resident Evil is also finding a new audience thanks to the new movie adaptation from horror director Zach Cregger, so what advice would they have for its unlucky hero, Bryan, as Resident Evil survivors?

"I'd probably say, find your version of Leon," says Sant'Albano. "Find your version of Leon, and try and find more than one bullet if you can, probably."

"Find a huge gun," adds Apostolides with a smile.

Sant'Albano is currently playing Hermia in A Midsummer Night's Dream (with added rave culture) at the Chichester Festival Theatre, while also working on adding her vocal talents to the King Arthur-meets-modern-day-apocalypse action-RPG Tides of Annihilation as hero Gwendolyn. Apostolides has a packed calendar too: he just did his first anime dub for Ghost in the Shell, is working on indie action-adventure RPG Emberville, and is developing his own game with his brother, a backyard-type zombie beat 'em up game inspired by his father. During the interview, he pitched an unusual role to Sant'Albano.

"You might have to play a zombie animal."

articles.title: Marvel's VisionQuest Series Kicks Off With a Solid Two-Episode Premiere, But It's James Spader's Ultron Who Steals the Show
articles.summary: VisionQuest may struggle a bit to reestablish the titular hero in this post-WandaVision MCU, but at least the series has James Spader’s Ultron to fall back upon. Read our spoiler-free review of the first two episodes.
articles.body:
The first two episodes of Marvel’s VisionQuest debut on Disney+ on Wednesday, October 14.

One of the most frustrating things about the post-Endgame MCU is how long it takes Marvel to circle back around and follow up on loose ends. Heck, they waited five years between Spider-Man sequels. And that’s to say nothing of the numerous post-credits scenes that still remain unresolved . VisionQuest is yet one more example of Marvel taking its sweet time to address a character who’s been trapped in storytelling limbo. Five years after WandaVision wrapped, we finally have a series dealing with the fate of Paul Bettany’s White Vision. But it’s not necessarily Vision himself who emerges as the beating heart of the series.

WandaVision is essentially the final leg of the trilogy begun by WandaVision in 2021 and continued by Agatha All Along in 2024 . When last we saw Bettany’s characters in the WandaVision finale, the regular Vision returned to blissful oblivion, while his emotionless clone fled Westview to ponder his own existence. Half a decade later, he’s still very much in the pondering phase. By day, works in a bar and struggles to master the nuances of human interaction. By night, he literally lives inside his own head in a fanciful construct populated by the various other Tony Stark-designed AI units. He’s a being who barely exists in the physical world any longer, until circumstances arise that force him back into action.

To be frank, as much as Bettany’s Vision is one of the best and most nuanced MCU characters, the series is a bit of a tough sell out of the gate. For one thing, the idyllic mansion construct feels like a rote, poor man’s recreation of what WandaVision was doing all those years ago, only without the TV sitcom conceit. It also feels like an attempted nod towards Tom King and Gabriel Hernandez Walta’s incredible 2015 Vision comic, though only in the most superficial sense. The production design in these scenes can't really be faulted, but there's nothing that WandaVision or Loki didn't do better in that regard.

On a deeper level, Vision is not at all the same character we’ve known and loved for the past 11 years. The old Vision, despite being a synthetic lifeform, was by far the most human and compassionate of the Avengers. He was responsible for some of the most poignant lines in the MCU. This new Vision utterly lacks that charm. He’s cold and distant. He doesn’t understand humans, much less feel any appreciation for their struggles and foibles. That’s the entire point of the series - the question of whether this carbon copy can gain the insight and emotional maturity that his predecessor possessed.

Regardless, this newer, less compassionate Vision is a harder character to connect with. Bettany certainly draws a firm distinction between the roles in his performance, but there’s just something a little off-putting about a Vision who shows such contempt for his fellow man and kills with abandon. By the end of Episode 2, that problem begins to recede somewhat, but there’s definitely a major adjustment period fans of the character will have to endure.

Luckily, if the series struggles to make its central protagonist fully resonate with viewers, it has a solid supporting cast to fall back upon. It’s a lot of fun seeing the various AI entities given “human” form inside Vision’s mind. That includes F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Orla Brady), E.D.I.T.H. (Emily Hampshire), and, best of all, the return of Agent Carter’s James D’Arcy to the J.A.R.V.I.S. role. Each character has been tasked with helping Vision understand humanity in one way or another, and all serve as entertaining foils to our dour hero.

Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

Then there’s the real highlight of the series in Episodes 1 and 2, James Spader’s Ultron. Say what you will about 2015’s Avengers: Age of Ultron, but Spader was an inspired casting choice, and this series promises to finally realize the lingering, untapped potential of that character in the MCU. Ultron is neither entirely friend nor foe to Vision, but more a cranky, supremely bored prisoner left over from a bygone era. Spader plays the role with gusto, bringing even more gravelly, affected charm to an AI who believes himself to be the smartest guy in every room. These episodes make the most of the role reversal, as now it’s Ultron who has something to teach Vision about the plight and beauty of mankind. If it’s tough to fully connect with Vision out of the gate, Ultron alone makes the series worth watching.

That’s not to say the series is devoid of any compelling human characters. Much as Agatha All Along marked the debut of the reincarnated Billy Maximoff (Joe Locke), VisionQuest focuses a great deal of attention on his brother Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica) and his own struggle to understand his existence and reconcile two very different sets of memories. Tommy makes for a compelling secondary protagonist in Episode 2, and its his presence that finally forces Vision to start coming out of his vibranium shell a bit.

On the villain front, these two episodes introduce us to Paladin (Todd Stashwick) and his handler (Diane Morgan). These two make for a fun pair, despite the fact that all of their interaction happens over the phone. In general, Stashwick brings plenty of campy energy to the screen, while at the same time molding his character into someone who feels like a legitimate threat to Vision despite the latter’s vastly superior powerset and refusal to engage in mind games.

articles.title: Epic Reportedly Pushing Devs to Use AI, Delays Secret Star Wars and Marvel Crossover Shooter
articles.summary: Epic Games has reportedly delayed its secret Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter as it pushes its developers to shift to an "AI first" production model.
articles.body:
Epic Games has reportedly delayed its secret Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter as it pushes its developers to shift to an "AI first" production model.

Details on the yet-to-be-announced Disney video game were shared by Bloomberg today. The site's report stated the untitled crossover experience was slated for release in March, but has since been pushed back to accommodate a new internal release plan that has yet to be shared.

Epic developers attached to the project have reportedly been encouraged to use tools such as Anthropic's AI assistant, Claude, with humans expected to oversee that work. Bloomberg also obtained an internal message shared by one of the Star Wars/Marvel game's directors.

Fortnite x Star Wars New Games and Rewards

"No more hand-written code,” an excerpt from the message said. The same message is then said to have added that all art for the project would be "generated with full AI workflows."

The report continued, stating that Epic underestimated the time and resources necessary to develop the Star Wars and Marvel shooter. Progress has been slower than expected, leading to the delay. When and where it will launch is unclear.

"We’re embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do," Epic communications director Jake Jones told Bloomberg in a statement.

The site added that Epic's push for what appears to be a project that leans heavily on AI left many of its developers "stunned." News of the Star Wars and Marvel shooter's schedule change follows another Bloomberg report from earlier this year, which stated that Epic was working on an extraction shooter featuring Disney characters . It was said to be similar to Embark Studios' Arc Raiders at the time.

Just moments before news of Epic's AI push broke, studio founder and CEO Tim Sweeney published a post on X/Twitter saying that the studio has a "huge pivot underway." He added that they are "moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration."

"The aim isn't to do the same stuff with fewer people," he continued, "but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal." In a follow-up post, Sweeney said , "Our more modest aim is to survive the AI revolution, help other developers do the same, and come out on the other end making better code and content faster."

"The biggest change will be much faster time from having an idea to playtesting it," he said in another post. "This will be great for gameplay, as most of the recent AAA failures can be attributed to game systems going through far too much of their development process without being able to playtest."

Disney purchased a $1.5 billion stake in the Fortnite developer in 2024 in a move that cemented their relationship at the time. Outside of more crossovers within Epic's still-popular battle royale-centered video game, it seems we've yet to see the extent of their collaborations. Meanwhile, Disney recently refuted claims that it was interested in outright acquiring the game studio .

articles.title: Teoscar Hernández moves up in the order for Game 2
articles.summary: Dave Roberts makes two changes, looking for a power spark in a lineup that didn’t get an extra-base hit in Game 1

After a series facing plenty of left-handers against the Braves, the Dodgers offense will see a second right-handed starter in Milwaukee. Although the scoring output was disappointing in Game 1, Dave Roberts sticks with his approach of righty-lefty throughout the lineup, but there are a couple of changes.

Tommy Edman, who was on the bench for Game 1, gets the starting nod over Kiké Hernández in the ninth spot, playing second base. This is Edman's first start since Game 2 of the NLDS, having appeared off the bench in each of the Dodgers' last three games. More notably, perhaps, Will Smith drops to the fifth spot in the order, with Teoscar Hernández moving up to bat third, rewarded for his two-hit performance in Game 1.

The Dodgers' starting catcher had more hard-hit balls than any other player in a 2-1 defeat—it just happened that they were all outs.

Mixing and matching late in games, expect either Josue De Paula or Kiké Hernández to be ready for an impact off the bench against a Brewers reliever, depending on which reliever is on the mound late in the game. De Paula in particular has impressed with key walks in this postseason.

articles.title: Student Suspended After Teachers Discover Death Note Notebook, Sparking Police Investigation
articles.summary: A student at a Massachusetts middle school found herself at the center of a police investigation after administrators discovered her Death Note notebook.
articles.body:
A student at a Massachusetts middle school found herself at the center of a police investigation after administrators discovered her Death Note notebook.

The incident took place at Chocksett Middle School in Sterling, Massachusetts. Students had already left for the day when staff discovered the notebook at around 4pm on September 30.

Police and school officials then conducted an investigation, interviewing both its owner and other students, and quickly determined that the Death Note — which contained a few names of its owner’s classmates — did not pose a legitimate threat. However, the student was suspended for three days.

“When we spoke with the student, the student explained that the notebook was connected to an anime television series and was not intended as a threat,” principal Tina Boss wrote in a letter addressed to the school’s community, adding that there was “no indication that the notebook or its contents were intended as a threat toward the school or any particular student.”

“Based on the information available at this time, the Sterling Police Department is not seeking criminal charges in connection with this incident,” the Sterling Police Department said in a press release.

Despite coming to this conclusion, police stood watch on the school grounds Tuesday, October 6, with officials saying it "will maintain a presence as it sees appropriate," as reported by local news outlet Boston.com .

A Death Note , in the anime of the same name, is a supernatural notebook owned by gods of death called shinigami. If someone writes the name of another person in the notebook, they will die. There are a few other rules , but that’s basically the gist of it.

Death Notes are often sold as merchandise for fans of the anime and manga series as basic notebooks with the 'Death Note' lettering on the front cover — but given the state of things in the United States over the last decade, it makes sense why parents and school administrators would be concerned for students’ safety after finding such a notebook. A mother of one of the children whose name was written in this particular Death Note expressed frustration with how the situation was handled on social media.

“A student who created a kill list with our daughter’s name on it is being allowed to return after just a three-day suspension… to the same classroom, within feet of her every day!” she wrote in a post on Facebook. “Yes, a safety plan is in place. But how does that plan give my daughter peace of mind when she still has to sit in the same classroom as the student who put her name on that list? She deserves to feel safe in her classroom, every single day.”

This isn’t the first time a student’s Death Note notebook has prompted such a reaction after being discovered at school; in September 2024, teachers at an I Promise school in Akron, Ohio were alerted after a student’s homemade ‘Death Note,’ written on sheets of loose leaf paper, was found. Although nothing came of the situation, parents of students whose names were written in the notebook similarly expressed dissatisfaction at how things were handled.

articles.title: Monaghan GAA: Former Armagh star John McEntee appointed Farney football boss
articles.summary: Former All-Ireland winner John McEntee is appointed Monaghan manager, replacing Gabriel Bannigan.
articles.body:
Former All-Ireland winner John McEntee has been appointed Monaghan manager, replacing Gabriel Bannigan.

McEntee, who helped Armagh win the Sam Maguire in 2002, takes his first inter-county job after spending the past four seasons in charge of Monaghan club Inniskeen.

The 49-year-old's appointment was ratified at a county board meeting on Monday night.

"I'm really excited and looking forward to it. Really privileged and honoured to be asked to take on this role and I'm going to give it my best shot," McEntee told Northern Sound.

"There's been conversations about the Monaghan post for a number of weeks since it became vacant and there were opportunities for clubs to put names forward.

"I didn't entertain that at the time because I was focused on Inniskeen but I knew this was naturally going to be the end of my tenure with Inniskeen and I had alternative options but this was the one that excited me the most."

He replaces Bannigan, who said "the goalposts have moved" when announcing his departure after two years at the helm in August.

After succeeding former Armagh team-mate Oisin McConville, McEntee led Inniskeen to Monaghan finals in 2023 and 2025, losing both to Scotstown.

He also oversaw Clontibret's 2019 Monaghan SFC triumph while he guided his club Crossmaglen Rangers to the Ulster title alongside McConville in 2015.

McEntee's twin brother Tony - with whom he won the All-Ireland title - spent the 2026 season in the Down backroom team following a spell as Sligo boss.

Under Bannigan, Monaghan won the Division Two title in 2025 and reached successive All-Ireland quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Donegal and Louth.

The Farney men were relegated from Division One this year after a tough league campaign in which they failed to pick up a point.

They bounced back well in the Ulster SFC with wins over Cavan and Derry but suffered an extra-time defeat against Armagh in the decider.

In the Sam Maguire series, Monaghan lost to eventual champions Mayo in round one but secured round 2B and three victories over Roscommon and Westmeath.

However, after losing influential goalkeeper Rory Beggan to injury, they fell to 0-27 to 2-18 loss to Louth in the quarter-final at Croke Park.

"I think there is a strong panel there with high quality players and it's a really good base to work from, but I think it's always good to bring talent through and I think that freshens up the squad," added McEntee.

"Gabriel left Monaghan in a really good place and we want to maintain those standards."

It was also confirmed on Monday that Tony Austin would take over as senior hurling boss after a spell in charge of club side Castleblayney, where he won four Monaghan SHC titles.

articles.title: Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew Wins Over Skeptical Fans With First Poster
articles.summary: The first poster for Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is here, and it seems to have won over a few of the more skeptical fans.
articles.body:
The first poster for Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is here, and it seems to have won over a few of the more skeptical fans.

Netflix shared an ethereal glimpse at the new Narnia movie on social media today. It came with the promise that a first look at the Barbie director's foray into the beloved fantasy universe will arrive via trailer tomorrow, though specifically when it will premiere is unclear.

The Narnia: The Magician's Nephew poster (below) seems to call back to art featured on some copies of author C. S. Lewis' original The Magician's Nephew novels. That would mean the three individuals illuminated by iridescent light here are Polly (Beatrice Campbell), Digory (David McKenna), and their flying horse, Fledge. The spacey lion gracing the background, meanwhile, teases Meryl Streep's Aslan.

The new poster for Gerwig's Netflix movie doesn't reveal much about its story or characters, but it's the look and feel that has fans taken aback. Even some of the more skeptical viewers, who have feared what an adaptation of Lewis' work would look like in 2026, like what they see here, with many taking to social media to praise the art.

"Well, that actually looks pretty awesome," one Reddit user said .

"Credit where credit is due, that is one hell of a poster," another added .

"It looks like a poster from a 1980s/early 1990s fantasy film and I am here for it," another user added .

That's not to say that there aren't still those who have yet to be impressed. Most of the concern seems to come from a place of dread that some of the most revered characters in fantasy could be warped or damaged on impact. Some naysayers are more vocal than others, but in reality, it's hard to say if Gerwig will land the plane just yet, but we'll definitely have a better idea when the film premieres next year.

"If I knew nooooothing else about this movie, I'd be excited," one of the more cautious fans said .

"I really like a lot of the visual stuff they’re doing with the movie," another explained . "Lots of cool filmic feeling stuff especially here. I just don’t like the time jump and the costume for Jadis doesn’t feel regal. It should be good technically but less so in other places."

In a relatively unlikely move from Netflix, Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is set to first come to theaters via IMAX sneak previews starting February 10, 2027. It will then receive a global wide release February 12, with streaming subscribers then able to watch from the comfort of their homes starting April 2.

Also included in the film's cast are Carey Mulligan, Daniel Craig, Emma Mackey, and Ciarán Hinds. While we wait to see how the movie may stray from the source material, you can check out more early details here . You can also check out what we learned after its logo reveal .

articles.title: Satisfactory: The Board Game Preview
articles.body:
Automation and factory-building games have become pretty popular over the past few years, with Coffee Stain Studios' Satisfactory being one of the stars of the genre. I have always admired the sprawling conveyor belts and mega structures of the factory-building powerhouse from a comfortable distance, dipping my toe into the waters with messy (but kind of functional) factories of my own. Soon, factory builders will have a whole new way to build out their process, as Mood Publishing, the same publisher behind Hitman: The Board Game , is looking to bring the beloved factory sim to your tabletop with Satisfactory: The Board Game and the launch of their latest crowdfunding campaign over on Gamefound . We were sent an early prototype copy to check out, in addition to playing a demo with the game’s designer, David Thor Fjalarsson, to see if a tabletop game can capture and refine the Satisfactory experience down to the size of a kitchen table-sized factory.

Satisfactory: The Board Game Preview Images

In Satisfactory: The Board Game (referred to simply as "Satisfactory" going forward), designed by David Thor Fjalarsson, up to four players will have to mine, refine, and upgrade their factories in an effort to earn the most FICSIT points before the space elevator is finished. The turns themselves are surprisingly straightforward; on your turn, you will perform two actions, either build something, move around the map, or have your factory do its work. Once each player has taken their turn, the production phase occurs, where everyone's mines will activate, drilling for one of the three basic materials—limestone, iron, or copper—and existing materials will move down their conveyors towards getting refined into better resources. Then, the whole cycle repeats itself. Even in my first game, by the time my group had reached the second or third round, we had the flow down.

The game itself takes place on a large hex-grid representation of the video game's massive world, with random creatures and biomes that get placed during setup, along with various material-rich points where mines can be placed. The “Move” action is pretty self-explanatory, allowing you to move your piece up to a number of spaces equal to your movement value, with some spaces that can only be crossed once certain technologies or vehicles have been built. Landing on a point can grant you resources, or allow you to claim one of the tokens mentioned earlier. If you prefer to get some extra work in at your factories, you can instead opt for the “Workshop” action, which lets you either move a beltline of resources down a spot or refine a single block of material into a higher-tier version, which is a crucial component for when you build.

Speaking of building things, the “Build” action was my favorite, and what I would consider the core thing to do in this game. At any time, players will have access to build their staple devices—extractors, refineries, et cetera—in addition to a random pool of cards of varying tiers that get unlocked over the course of the game. These cards, like the Jet Pack to help you get around quicker or weapons to tackle the wildlife, are a great help, but the main structures you can construct have an added little treat to them. Depending on what you build, you will have a bonus action that you can take, determined by what you have built. Building a miner, for instance, will allow you to immediately build a Belt, which will then trigger the Belt’s bonus, giving you a free movement action, or the Constructor, giving you an extra action you can take on your turn. Stringing together these bonuses to create some wild turns was some of the most fun I had playing Satisfactory.

When it comes to playing, Satisfactory's tabletop adaptation has opted for a competitive “race for points” experience for its main game, instead of the cooperative focus from the PC title — though the promised final game will include a co-op and solo modes as well. That said, don't expect to be bombing or taking out the other players' extractors and belts with some cardboard corporate terrorism within the game. Instead, once a player has claimed a tile by building something on it, no other player can develop on it, though they can still cross over with no issue. Satisfactory can still be “mean,” but it’s more like cleverly getting in the way or making expansion for your opponents annoying as opposed to turning the planet into a battlefield.

This sort of headbutting really only comes out when you start getting to the three- or four-player counts. At two players, because both players have so much more space, I was surprised and impressed with how different Satisfactory manages to feel. During my two-player game, with far less worry about my factory getting locked in by other players, I instead was able to focus and work out how best I wanted to try and optimize (as optimized as you could get in a game like this after only a couple plays) my system. It honestly felt like I was playing different games based on the player counts, with two players focusing on optimizing and planning out turns to maximize earning points, while with three, and especially four, figuring out how best to expand my factory and balancing blocking resources from the others was much more in the forefront of my mind. Oddly enough, I think I actually enjoyed the puzzley nature of the lower player count more, as both of us weren’t forced into conflict with one another, and I could better test out what Satisfactory offers.

In one two-player game, I focused on maxing out my basic resource production, getting all of my extractors online as fast as I could, and expanding my reach to a few farther-out “rich” tiles, which further let me produce more of the resource during production phases. Having an almost overabundance of these cheaper resources allowed me to quickly gobble up and complete the early-game Milestones, netting me a bunch of points and rocketing me out into the lead, faster than the elevator could take me. During one particularly memorable event, thanks to the rewards given by completing the goals and what I had earned from various Biomes I visited that turn, I was able to complete four of the Milestones back -to-back-to-back. It was a straight dopamine shot to the system, and basically sold me on Satisfactory alone.

I, admittedly, approached Satisfactory from the viewpoint of someone who hasn’t sunk all that many hours into the game that it has been adapted from, but even this condensed package still manages to FEEL like Satisfactory. Watching my pathways of conveyor belts expand outwards across the map, discovering alternate recipes, and building the network of machines to allow me to continue to refine my goods and open up new technologies is still all here. Even memorable critters like Bean are here. There are plenty of other nods that longtime players will pick up on better than I, but I applaud the designers for still managing to make this feel like Satisfactory at its heart. The tabletop adaptation obviously can’t replicate the massive, near-limitless scale of the PC game, but it looks to have successfully mined what matters most: building an efficient system and then riding it until you need to upgrade it to reach loftier heights.

If there is one thing that interested builders should be aware of, it is that Satisfactory is not a small game. It requires a good bit of table space to play, and it will assault you with icons. When its multiple boards, piles of cards, large play board, and resource tokens are all laid out, this is a surprisingly imposing tabletop experience. Some smart decisions, such as keeping the material types down to just three, do help keep you from being overwhelmed by resource management, thankfully. Frankly, keeping track of and remembering what all the icons meant was more of a hassle than managing my stockpiles of colored cubes.

Different icons appear all over the place, on cards, on the map, the player boards, and even the victory point track, and at least in the prototype I had, it did not come with a player reference card. Thankfully, I’ve been assured there is one that will come with the release copy, which should alleviate some of that headache of keeping track of what means what. It took the better part of the game to grasp the icons, but by the end, it did start clicking, and again, much of that pain will be lessened with the inclusion of a reference card.

Satisfactory: The Board Game is still being tweaked and adjusted, but Mood appears to have succeeded in shrinking down the complex factory-building game and distilling it down to its raw materials to create a surprisingly approachable (if not a bit intimidating-looking) board game. The limited action choices you have on your turn help keep turns quick and snappy, but I can certainly see how, if you have a tendency to hyper-analyze your turns or have to make the most optimized play, turns could easily take a bit longer. Regardless, the implementation here, adapting so many systems while still being a game that doesn’t take all day to play (my games usually lasted 2 - 3.5 hours), is impressive. Thankfully, before backing the game, a draft version of the rules has been posted along with the full list of add-ons and what is included in the pledge tiers over on the Gamefound page . Or, better yet, you and your game group can try it for yourselves in Tabletop Simulator on Steam using an official preview build mod made by MOOD! Now, back to trying to figure out how to build my own mega factory.

Scott White is a freelance contributor to IGN, assisting with tabletop games and guide coverage. Follow him on X/Twitter or Bluesky .

articles.title: Yelich's huge two-run hit gives Brewers lead, drives out Yamamoto
articles.summary: After Jake Bauers worked a 12-pitch walk to load the bases, Christian Yelich hit a two-run single to give the Brewers a 3-2 lead in the third inning.
articles.body:
What a third inning and what a moment for the Milwaukee Brewers .

After falling behind the Los Angeles Dodgers , 2-1, in the top of the inning, they took the lead, 3-2, in the bottom with a big hit from their captain.

Christian Yelich hit a two-out single with the bases loaded to drive in two runs and drive Dodgers starter Yoshi Yamamoto out of the game. Yamamoto threw 36 pitches in the inning alone and finished with 75.

Yelich got the glory but the absolute star of the inning was Jake Bauers, who worked a 12-pitch walk that seemed to build with every delivery.

A couple were pop-ups that Dodgers defenders couldn't quite chase down in foul territory, and Bauers wound up getting on base to load them up.

It's the most pitches Yamamoto has thrown in any MLB appearance in his career.

Brewers vs Dodgers highlights, National League Championship Series Game 2

To start the inning, David Hamilton singled, Jackson Chourio flew out, Brice Turang walked – despite another pitch that would have been strike three if the Dodgers had asked for an ABS replay – and William Contreras flew out. All the at-bats were lengthy.

That brought up Bauers, followed by Yelich, who didn't have a single playoff RBI dating to Game 7 of the 2018 series before getting three now this year.

Brewers fans tailgate at American Family Field before NLCS Game 2

articles.summary: Universal cables perfect for your Switch 2, Steam Deck, or iPhone 18.
articles.body:
USB Type-C has become the standard for charging and data cables alike, so it's good to have extra on hand. Amazon is offering a two-pack of Ainope 6.6ft 60W Right Angle USB-C Cables for just $4.99 after you apply coupon code " 658Q94W5 ". That averages out to $2.50 per cable.

USB-C cables typically go for about $10 each at your local big box store, and can be used to charge or sync any USB-C device, including your Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or iPhone 17.

2-Pack of Ainope Right Angle 6.6ft USB-C Cables for $5

2-Pack Ainope 6.6ft 60W Right Angle USB C to USB C Cable

Keep your cable collection simple. These cables measure 6.6 feet in length, which is a great general purpose length: long enough to still be able to use your device while the cable is plugged in, but not so long as to be an unnecessary nuisance. These cables are also rated for up to 60W of power delivery, which is sufficient for the vast majority of your portable electronics, including smartphones, tablets, and all handheld gaming PCs .

A rather unique feature of this cable is that one end has a right-angle connector. This is useful if you don't want that end to protrude too much, thus minimizing accidental wear and tear, or worse, breakage. The cables are encased in a nylon braid for extra durability and aeshetics, while the terminals are profesionally sheathed in hard plastic boots. Customers appear to be satisfied; the cables have over 37,000 reviews on Amazon with an average 4.6 star rating.
